item.title: Using Artificial Intelligence to Improve Diabetes Medication Safety After Hospital Discharge
item.description:
# Using Artificial Intelligence to Improve Diabetes Medication Safety After Hospital Discharge A newly funded project led by **Alok Kapoor, MD**, will explore how artificial intelligence can help people with diabetes better understand changes to their medications when leaving the hospital.
The project, funded by the [Herman G. Berkman Diabetes Clinical Innovation Fund](https://www.umassmed.edu/dcoe/diabetes-research/clinical-innovation-fund/), will develop and test an interactive artificial intelligence tool using a communication technique known as teach-back.
Using a secure artificial intelligence system restricted to carefully selected, safety-focused information, the tool will generate questions based on each patient's diabetes medication instructions.
A clinician will be present during all patient testing to identify and correct any errors made by the artificial intelligence tool.
## [Using Artificial Intelligence to Improve Diabetes Medication Safety After Hospital Discharge](https://www.umassmed.edu/dcoe/diabetes-care/artificial-intelligence-to-improve-medication-safety/) This project will develop and test an artificial intelligence tool designed to help patients better understand changes to their diabetes medications when leaving the hospital.
## [AI Diabetic Retinopathy Screening in Primary Care](https://www.umassmed.edu/dcoe/umass-diabetes-news/2023/01/berkman/) This project implemented an artificial intelligence (AI)- based diabetic retinopathy screening program in Family Medicine clinics to detect eye disease and improve comprehensive care for people living with diabetes.
